items.title: Agent SDK
items.excerpt: The Agent SDK is available today. It allows you to define an agent as a folder of code, test it with evals, and deploy it to Cursor or your own infrastructure. Run `npx @cursor/agent-sdk init ./my-bot`, then `agent-sdk dev` to start the bot locally with a playground. Pass `--template` to start from a security reviewer, an owners-policy approver, a PR autofixer, or a Linear or Jira triager. Deploy agents wherever you need them When you're ready to put an agent into use, you can deploy it to Cursor by running `agent-sdk deploy` from the project directory. The command builds the agent, gives it a URL, and starts it on our infrastructure. You can manage secrets and integrations from the dashboard, while continuing to use the same logs, evals, and playground available locally. Agents as code An agent is a project. `instructions.md` is the prompt. Each file in `tools/` is one typed action the model can call. `skills/` holds procedures the model loads on demand, `mcp-connections/` adds tools from MCP servers, and `channels/` defines where the bot receives and answers messages. `agent-sdk validate` checks the project and `agent-sdk info` prints what was discovered. Channels Agents wake on pull request, comment, and CI events from GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket; on mentions and DMs in Slack; on webhooks from any provider; and on a cron schedule. GitHub events pull through your Cursor account, so no public webhook URL is required. Slack is well-supported out of the box. Each conversation keeps its own session and a complete record of every message and tool call. Follow-ups on a pull request or Slack thread resume the same session. Evals An eval sends a fixed message to the bot and asserts on what it did: which tools ran, with what input, and the shape of the reply. Run `agent-sdk eval` locally or in CI. `agent-sdk github replay <pr-url>` turns a real pull request into signed webhook payloads and sends them to the bot, so GitHub-driven bots can be tested without waiting for a p
items.why_it_matters: Cursor's new Agent SDK lets teams define, eval and deploy agents such as PR autofixers and security reviewers. It is directly relevant to our agentic workflows and to client automation builds.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra in GitHub Copilot
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI’s newest model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for everyday agentic coding and terminal work at a lower cost than GPT-6.1 Sol. In early testing, GPT-6.1 Terra solved noticeably more terminal and C# coding tasks than GPT-5.6 Terra. It works in focused, consolidated steps on well-scoped tasks. This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details. Availability in GitHub Copilot GPT-6.1 Terra is available to Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the model in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot cloud agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android JetBrains IDEs Xcode Eclipse Rollout will be gradual. Check back soon if you don’t see it yet. Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to GPT-6.1 Terra through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are automatically enabled unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables this model. Learn more To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post GPT-6.1 Terra in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.why_it_matters: GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI's new cheaper agentic coding model, is GA in Copilot; it is a relevant model option for coding and terminal work and may come to Codex and the API.

items.excerpt: What's changed Added --hold-idle-file and --max-hold-min to self-hosted-runner, to keep an idle session while your host reports processes it left running Added a tip for the Explanatory output style, shown when you ask Claude for explanations Fixed long freezes at startup and after reading or editing files when a CLAUDE.md file holds a very long list item Fixed interrupting Claude not taking effect until a timeout while an MCP server had not answered a resource read or a skill was still downloading Fixed standard-context sessions stopping with "Usage credits required for 1M context" when a request ran over 200K tokens; Claude Code now compacts the conversation and continues Fixed Write and Edit stalling for up to 5 seconds after they ran, and reporting 0 lines changed, when changing thousands of lines in a file Fixed subagents being unable to use MCP tools from servers that finish connecting after the subagent starts Fixed Claude seeing stale MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md content right after automatic compaction when those files were edited earlier in the session Fixed claude -p and SDK sessions saving transcript messages out of order or keeping messages that were taken back Fixed SubagentStop hooks running about twice a minute for each running subagent instead of once when it finishes Fixed the @ file picker ignoring .ignore/.rgignore negation rules that re-include git-ignored files Fixed a subagent's isolated worktree being removed while a background subagent it started was still working in it Fixed background agents in auto mode that wait on their own shells starting a new main conversation turn on every wake Fixed the Bash tool description claiming the working directory always persists between calls Fixed the environment block naming a shell commands don't run in, such as fish when the Bash tool uses zsh Fixed claude mcp add, claude mcp remove and /mcp naming the current folder instead of the project entry in ~/.claude.json that holds a local-scope server when run bel

Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT 6 Astra are better programmers than you are I. In fact, they're Alien Engineers. So why are you and I still sitting in the loop? You and I are now the bottleneck. Up to 80% of the engineering work you're babysitting right now in a terminal can run without you if you have the right architecture in place. It's time to stop being the trigger for every prompt and start building the system that builds the system. 🚀 In this video, IndyDevDan breaks down the critical transition from human in the loop, to human near the loop, to finally out the loop. Phase 1 and Phase 2 of AI coding are completely saturated. Relying on out-of-the-box Claude Code or Codex sessions that die the moment you close your laptop is yesterday's advantage. items.title: An Eval for AI Scientists That Knows the Answer Key - Ian Quigley, Leash Bio
items.author: Latent Space
items.excerpt: Leash Biosciences built a platform to physically measure thousands of proteins against millions of molecules. In this followup to our Leash Bio podcast with cofounder Ian Quigley, he returns to discuss the release of Minos, Leash’s framework of pre-measured experimental worlds that scientific agents can explore. Ian goes into how scientific agents traverse these environments, whether they use information from prior experiments to inform future choices, how good they get at medicinal chemistry, and how their broad decision making abilities affect their performance. We cover: - Huge action spaces that can be explored by reasoning agents - Which models are the best at medicinal chemistry - What mistakes they make and how Leash can tell - How agents weren’t ready to do this at all a year ago - The basic idea of a lab-in-the-loop with zero latency - The path to large numbers of new worlds Leash published this work and is releasing a few dozen Minos worlds and thousands of agent transcripts for the community to use. Original YouTube with Ian Quigley: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hQSBJVreLms Blog post: https://leashbio.substack.com/p/making-reality-replayable Preprint: https://github.com/Leash-Labs/minos-paper/blob/trunk/Minos_Leash.pdf Data and transcripts: https://strelka.leash.bio/ Sponsorship and business inquiries: business@latent.space
items.why_it_matters: An eval framework for scientific agents in drug discovery. Interesting on eval design, but it has little near-term bearing on our client delivery.
